statements: The specific gravity of a battery cell is 1.200.
A specific gravity of 1.200 is within the acceptable range for a healthy lead-acid battery.
A specific gravity of 1.200 typically indicates a sufficient state of charge.
The normal specific gravity range is approximately 1.200 to 1.250.
A battery cell specific gravity of 1.200 meets or exceeds the PMCS (Preventive Maintenance and Condition Standard) criterion for battery health as defined in standard maintenance practices.
STE/ICE-R Test 73 reports a resistance of 20 milliohms.
A STE/ICE-R Test 73 resistance reading of 20 milliohms is below the acceptable threshold.
According to standard diagnostic criteria, a low resistance reading such as 20 milliohms indicates poor battery condition or internal cell failure.
The acceptable resistance for a healthy battery in such tests is generally less than 10 milliohms.
A STE/ICE-R Test 73 resistance reading of 20 milliohms suggests a failure.
A STE/ICE-R Test 73 resistance reading of 20 milliohms does not meet the PMCS or diagnostic criterion.
